title: Validate multipart boundaries and enforce file-size/content-type limits on OpenAI-compat tool/file endpoints
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: several incidents and flaky E2E runs showed that tool/file uploads to the OpenAI-compat endpoints could hang or be accepted with malformed boundaries or incorrect content-type headers, leading to streaming stalls and memory spikes on private deployments. This PR tightens validation for multipart/form-data and chunked transfer uploads, adds enforcement of default file-size limits, and surfaces explicit compatibility-layer error codes so downstream SDKs and clients can handle rejections cleanly. Summary of changes: - Add a multipart boundary presence and consistency check early in request parsing; reject requests missing a boundary with 422 MALFORMED_MULTIPART. - Enforce Content-Type whitelist for tool/file payloads (application/octet-stream, image/*, text/*, application/json, multipart/form-data). Requests with disallowed content-types now return 400 INVALID_CONTENT_TYPE. - Introduce Content-Length and chunked streaming guards. For chunked uploads we now apply per-chunk size ceiling and an aggregate max (default 25MB) and return 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE when exceeded. Limit is configurable via service config and Dedicated/Private can override per-tenant. - Update the OpenAI-compat adapter to normalize incoming form-data to internal file objects, while preserving streaming semantics. Old behavior accepted missing boundary on some clients; new behavior rejects those requests but includes a compatibility hint header (X-Compat-Error) to aid callers. - Add a small in-memory streaming parser for boundary edge-cases to avoid allocating large buffers when boundaries come in split TCP frames. - Bake in tests: unit tests for malformed boundary paths, integration tests with chunked transfer encoding (nginx-style split chunks), e2e test that runs against the compatibility layer. - Documentation: api changelog + compatibility notes and SDK test expectations. Risk & rollout: - Backwards compatible at the protocol level for well-formed clients; some malformed clients will be rejected. To soften rollout we emit the X-Compat-Error hints and a telemetry metric (compat.multipart.reject_count) for 2 weeks before flipping enforcement in some private installs where customers asked for a grace period. - Default file-size cap is conservative (25MB); customers can configure via config.service.file_upload.max_size_bytes. Related: ENG-4132 (multipart resilience), PM-291 (compat ergonomics).

release_notes:
- Enforce multipart boundary and return 422 MALFORMED_MULTIPART for missing/mismatched boundaries.
- Enforce allowed content-types on tool/file endpoints (400 INVALID_CONTENT_TYPE).
- Default file upload size cap of 25MB with 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE error for overage (configurable).
- Compatibility layer emits X-Compat-Error header to help client migration.
notes: This is primarily an API-surface hardening PR. Product notified SDK teams to add handling for new error tokens. Metric compat.multipart.reject_count configured to surface rejections during initial rollout.
backout_plan: Revert the adapter normalization commit and disable enforcement flag using runtime feature toggle. Telemetry events will be used to identify affected clients before rollback.
testing_instructions:
- Run unit tests: cargo test --workspace -p http-server
- Run integration: ./scripts/run_chunked_integration.sh
- E2E: run compatibility suite against staging cluster (see docs/api/compatibility/file_uploads.md)
